input: Volunteer at the animal shelter every other Saturday

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing which shelter (or whether one has been chosen yet) determines whether the first step is finding/applying to a shelter or simply scheduling shifts at an existing one.
Knowing the start date pins down the first Saturday and establishes which Saturdays are 'on' vs 'off' going forward.
Understanding the preferred time slot (morning, afternoon, full day) affects scheduling around other commitments and what roles are feasible.
Knowing if this is solo or with others (friend, family, partner) changes sign-up logistics, coordination steps, and accountability.
Hard limits like transport, physical ability, or competing recurring commitments directly affect which shelter, shift, and role are realistic.
The type of volunteer work preferred (animal handling, cleaning, admin, events) determines which roles to seek and what training may be needed.
Knowing what 'sticking with it' looks like — a trial period, a year-long commitment, or indefinite — shapes how to build in reminders, accountability, and review points.

gold.taskTitle: Volunteer at animal shelter every other Saturday
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to establish a recurring every-other-Saturday volunteering routine at an animal shelter.

questions.title: Have you already chosen a specific shelter?
questions.description: Determines whether the first step is researching and applying to a shelter or scheduling at one already selected.

questions.title: Which Saturday do you want to start?
questions.description: Pins down the first shift date so the every-other-Saturday rhythm can be set correctly from the beginning.

questions.title: What time of day works best for your shifts?
questions.description: Clarifies whether you are targeting a morning, afternoon, or full-day slot each volunteering Saturday.

questions.title: Will you be volunteering alone or with someone?
questions.description: Determines whether sign-up and coordination steps need to account for one person or a group.

questions.title: Do you have reliable transport to get to the shelter?
questions.description: Identifies any hard logistical constraints around travel that could affect which shelter is realistic to commit to.

questions.title: What kind of volunteer work do you most want to do?
questions.description: Establishes whether you prefer hands-on animal care, cleaning and kennel work, front-desk or admin support, or outreach events.

questions.title: How long are you aiming to keep this commitment?
questions.description: Defines the intended duration — a short trial, a fixed number of months, or an open-ended ongoing routine — so accountability checkpoints can be built in.
